analysis: Documentation-only changes reviewed. The docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md head line 621 adds Gemma4TensorParallelPrefix.scopes to the list of helpers that apply the tenant-scoped cluster prefix SSD records (|tenant= plus the salt's SHA-256 digest). The other change is a date bump at line 3. The docs/provider/two-mac-cluster.md head lines 486-490 now describe Gemma 4 tensor-parallel prefix keeping. Each Mac keeps its own half of each layer's heads. A prefix is restored only when both Macs hold it. Lines 520-525 state that prefixes are kept per tenant on both Macs. Head lines 336-353 add a placement table and Gemma TP planner prose; these lines are not in the supplied unit, but the patch excerpt shows them and they are not security-relevant. Relevant threat: T-041 (tenant scope folded into the chain hash and HMAC tag; cross-account isolation; SEC-035 accepted residual). The docs claim the Gemma4 TP path follows the same ClusterWorkerPrefixCache scope contract. No weakening of TTL, KEK, HMAC naming, AAD, kill switch or tenant isolation is described. The Swift implementation of Gemma4TensorParallelPrefix.scopes is not supplied. Integration should verify that it uses ClusterWorkerPrefixCache.scope and honors 'disabled' and no-salt requests. It should also confirm that the documented 'no reuse' behavior for requests without a Darkbloom cache scope holds for Gemma TP (two-mac-cluster.md line 522). There is an apparent tension with the ssd-kv-cache.md table row 'None (cache on, no salt)', which reads 'read and written as before'; integration should reconcile the two. That row is unchanged in this PR, so this is a question rather than a regression. No findings, because no security behavior change is evidenced in the supplied docs.
